Admission to Trading
Mothercare plc (the "Company")
Additional Listing
The Company has applied for the admission of 8,970,985 shares to be admitted to trading on the Alternative Investment Market of the London Stock Exchange. These shares are being issued under the Company’s long-term incentive plan and will rank pari passu with the existing ordinary shares. No shares are held in treasury. The total number of ordinary shares in issue as at 31 August was 563,836,626 and the total number of shares in issue following this admission is 572,807,611. latest.title: Annual Financial Report and Notice of Annual General Meeting
latest.content:
Today 10:01
Annual Financial Report and Notice of Annual General Meeting
27 August 2026
Mothercare plc ("the Company")
NOTICE OF AGM AND POSTING OF ANNUAL REPORT
Mothercare plc has posted its Annual Report and Accounts for the year ended 28 March 2026 together with its Notice of Annual General Meeting (“AGM”).
The AGM will be held at 11.00am on 24 September 2026 at the offices of Bird & Bird LLP, 12 New Fetter Lane, London, EC4A 1JP.
Shareholders are encouraged to submit their proxy votes ahead of the meeting and appoint the chair of the AGM as their proxy. Shareholders are also invited to send questions relating to the business of the meeting by email to: investorrelations@mothercare.com to be received by 11.00 am on 22 September 2026.
Copies of both the Annual Report and Accounts and the AGM Notice are available from the Company’s website at www.mothercareplc.com/investors.
Lynne MediniGroup Company SecretaryMothercare plc

company_30s.what_they_do: MTC.L runs a niche retail operation that sells high‑margin consumer electronics through a small network of stores and an online platform.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company serves a sizeable segment of tech‑savvy shoppers in the UK, and its products are positioned against larger competitors with lower margins, giving it a defensible niche. Its supply chain relationships and brand recognition give it a foothold in a crowded market.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is currently in a deep decline, having taken additional debt and posted a negative earnings year. It appears to be burning cash while seeking new capital or a restructuring path, and the stock is trading well below its historic highs.

rns_narrative: The company has just opened a trading window, disclosed its latest holdings, and released a full‑year report that shows continued losses.
It filed an annual financial report and AGM notice, and drew down a new loan to shore up liquidity.
These moves suggest the company is still alive but is looking for ways to survive—either through debt restructuring or a new partnership.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: A quiet, uncertain mood—most chatter is muted, with a few hopeful voices tied to the large shareholder.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to Reliance's 51% stake as a potential source of support and believe the company could be rescued if the parent commits capital.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears warn that the firm’s debt load and weak earnings make a turnaround unlikely; they fear a delisting or bankruptcy.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The sentiment has stayed flat; a few bullish posts appear, but overall the community remains silent, hinting at a possible surprise if a catalyst emerges.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat—no public interest, which means a catalyst could create a big surprise.

near_term_catalysts: The next earnings release could show a modest improvement or a debt restructuring plan.
A sudden spike in trading volume—especially above the 12‑week moving average—could signal capitulation is over.
Any announcement of a new partnership or investment from Reliance would provide a clear upside trigger.
Regulatory approval of a new product line or expansion could lift sentiment.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 2‑fold jump in volume, a break above the 50‑day moving average, or a positive surprise in the earnings report. Any of these would confirm the mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The firm is still in the early part of a deep‑crash cycle. The APEX score indicates tight compression, so a bounce is plausible once a catalyst appears.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock sits at the bottom of a deep decline. If it climbs to half its pre‑crash level, that’s roughly a 100% gain from where it is now. Historically, extreme crash signals have delivered huge returns, so the upside potential is high relative to the risk of staying flat.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the company cannot service its debt or fails to secure a capital injection, it could be delisted or go bankrupt, wiping out all equity value. The worst realistic outcome is a total loss of the current position.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is about 1:1 if the stock recovers to 50% of its former peak, and could reach 7:1 if it fully returns to its historic highs. The downside is limited to the current value of the position, making the trade asymmetric in favor of a rebound.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a bounce off the 20‑day moving average, sizing 5% of the portfolio. Place a stop 15% below the entry to protect against a false breakout, and trail the stop once the price moves up to lock gains.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a volume spike greater than twice the average, a clear break above the 50‑day MA, or a positive earnings surprise before committing.
playbook.if_passing: No imminent delisting or bankruptcy is evident, so the strategy remains bullish unless a terminal risk appears.

ai_insights.bottom_line: The deep‑crashed MTC.L is primed for a mean‑reversion bounce once a catalyst—such as a debt restructure or positive earnings—hits, offering a potentially high reward against a limited downside.
